$comment: ★ DELIBERATELY CONTENT-FREE — DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY PADDING IT OUT. Neutral shipped <sys/sysctl.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. THE HEADER EXISTS SO THAT AN #include OF IT RESOLVES; it deliberately publishes no CTL_* / HW_* / KERN_* constant and no struct. WHY, stated so a later reader does not mistake this for an oversight: (1) THE FUNCTIONS ARE ALREADY SHIPPED AND ALREADY EXPORT-VERIFIED ELSEWHERE — `sysctl` at unistd.json:42 and `sysctlbyname` at unistd.json:43, both gated [macho], both confirmed present in libSystem by a real dlopen+dlsym run on an actual Mac (recorded at .plans/_deferred-anchor-registry.md:740). sqlite reaches sysctlbyname by name only; re-declaring either here would plant a SECOND eager import of the same symbol for no gain. (2) ★ THE CORPUS USAGE, RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE RATHER THAN INHERITED — the hand-off note for this work said 'no CTL_*/HW_* constant is referenced'. THAT IS WRONG, and the correction is recorded here because it changes who is affected. A grep over the whole staged tree ($HOME/src/sqlite) finds `src/test1.c:9100-9103` using the MIB-ARRAY form: `nm[0] = CTL_HW; nm[1] = HW_AVAILCPU;` then `nm[1] = HW_NCPU;`. THE CLI IS STILL UNAFFECTED, which is why this file ships content-free NOW: `sqlite3.c:28345` uses the NAME-based `sysctlbyname("hw.ncpu", &cpuCount, &len, NULL, 0)`, which needs no constant at all, and `shell.c` references none — so `sqlite3` builds. THE TESTFIXTURE IS AFFECTED: a macho build of `src/test1.c` will fail LOUD (S0001, undefined `CTL_HW`/`HW_AVAILCPU`/`HW_NCPU`) the moment it is attempted, because a descriptor SHADOWS the real header and this one publishes nothing. That is a fail-loud gap, not a silent one, and it is the named, in-tree consumer that gives D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY its priority — it is no longer hypothetical. (3) WE CANNOT MEASURE THE REAL VALUES HERE. The SDK slice this cycle worked from (/tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include) carries only sys/{fcntl,file,mount,param,syslimits}.h + malloc/malloc.h — sys/sysctl.h is NOT in it. The CTL_* namespace is 4.4BSD-derived and *looks* portable, which is exactly what makes guessing it dangerous: a descriptor SHADOWS the real header TOTALLY (include_path_resolve.hpp:60-75, Descriptor → Source → NotFound), including on a NATIVE macOS host where the SDK header is used today via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK, so a wrong MIB constant would not fail to compile — it would query the WRONG kernel node at runtime and return a plausible number. A partial-but-correct surface is a fail-loud gap; a complete-but-guessed surface is a silent wrong answer. We take the gap, and we ANCHOR it: D-FFI-DARWIN-SYSCTL-CONSTANTS-EMPTY (closing work: measure CTL_*/HW_*/KERN_* + `struct sysctl_oid`-adjacent shapes against a real SDK, then ship the closed domains whole). ★ WHY THERE IS A MACRO HERE AT ALL: the loader REFUSES a descriptor that declares nothing (shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp:2188-2199 — 'declares nothing — needs at least one of symbols, constants, floatConstants, typedefs, structs, unions, or macros'), so a literally empty file cannot ship. The include guard is the one declaration the real header unambiguously makes and no consumer branches on it. `_SYS_SYSCTL_H_` follows the Darwin `_SYS_<NAME>_H_` convention MEASURED across every sibling in the slice (sys/mount.h → _SYS_MOUNT_H_, sys/param.h → _SYS_PARAM_H_, sys/file.h → _SYS_FILE_H_, sys/fcntl.h → _SYS_FCNTL_H_, sys/syslimits.h → _SYS_SYSLIMITS_H_) — the convention is measured, this specific name is INFERRED from it. ★ NO `symbols` AND NO `library` KEY, BY DESIGN: DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists, so an unexported name breaks EVERY binary's LOAD (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT, macho exit 127) — with none declared, the blast radius of including this header is exactly nil. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); Linux's sysctl(2) is deprecated and its MIB values differ, so an elf build must never silently pick this up.
